sentences: In a field under a high blue sky, a half-clothed woman holding a basket turns her head to look straight at us.
Beside her stands a girl with bobbed hair in a sleeveless dress, while drooping sunflowers, corn and reeds turn yellow around them.
The clothes say midsummer but the landscape says autumn, because Yi In-seong posed the figures from a photograph taken in Daegu in August 1933 and painted the scenery later that autumn.

The bold primary colours, decorative layout and the woman's stiff pose recall Gauguin, yet the two figures are the painter's own younger sisters and the same basket appears in his still life Roses from that year.
Born into a poor family in Daegu, Yi first learned watercolour from the painter Seo Dong-jin, and won a special prize with this painting at the 13th Joseon Art Exhibition in 1934.
It is often called the fullest expression of the 'Korean local colour' debated in the 1930s, though some critics fault it for picturing colonial Korea as a fragile woman and child.
The next year Yi took the exhibition's top prize, and he died in 1950, only thirty-eight.
